test_title: SSC Stenographer 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 10 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Six rights guaranteed by Article 19 can be suspended on the grounds of:

1. War

2. External aggression

3. Armed rebellion

4. Internal disturbance
solution:
The correct answer is __**1 and 2 both**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **six fundamental rights guaranteed by Article 19 **of the Indian Constitution **can be suspended on the grounds of war or external aggression**. 
 
• The** 44th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1978** amended the Constitution to allow the suspension of the six rights under Article 19 only in the case of war or external aggression. 
 
• The **suspension of the rights is automatic when a national emergency is declared under Article 358. **
 
• The suspension of the rights does not require a separate order from the President. 
 
• The rights are automatically restored after the emergency ends. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Article 19 deals with the six Fundamental Rights. They are:

 
 
• Right to freedom of speech and expression.
 
• Right to assemble peacefully and without arms.
 
• Right to form association or unions or co-operatives.
 
• Right to move freely throughout the territory of India.
 
• Right to reside and settle in any part of the territory of India.
 
• Right to practice any profession or to carry on any occupation, trade or business.
